title: Finite geometric image of a rank-one Weil character on a curve
statement:
Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be normal, geometrically connected,
separated and of finite type,
pure of dimension one. Put
$U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and
$\Pi=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$. Let $\ell\nmid q$, let
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let

$$
\chi:\hyperref[def-wf-weil-group]{W(U_0,\bar u)}\longrightarrow E^\times
$$

be a continuous character. Then $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite. Equivalently,
there is $N\geq1$ such that $\chi(g)^N=1$ for every $g\in\Pi$.
The scheme and Weil-group conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-wf-weil-group].

proof.text: The hypotheses on $U_0$ allow [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence]; its surjectivity gives $s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ with $\deg(s)=1$. By [lem-wf-compact-character-logarithm], choose $N\geq1$ and the continuous additive character $\lambda(g)=\log(\chi(g)^N):\Pi\to E$, invariant under $g\mapsto s^{-1}gs$. Every $\chi(g)^N$ lies in the stated logarithm domain $1+\ell^2\mathcal O_E$. We use exactly this domain clause, rather than any unstated condition on the lemma's auxiliary integer $r$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: degree-one lift and invariant logarithm

proof.text: By [def-galois-fibre-functor], $\Pi$ is the automorphism group of a finite-set-valued functor on a chosen small skeleton, with the evaluation topology. Hence [lem-galois-aut-profinite] makes $\Pi$ profinite, in particular compact. Choose a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-basis of $E$ and its coordinate maps $t_i:E\to\mathbf Q_\ell$. They are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous]: the scalar field $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is complete and nontrivially valued, and the finite extension $E$ is a finite-dimensional Hausdorff topological vector space with its valuation topology. Thus $f_i=t_i\circ\lambda$ are continuous additive characters, still conjugation-invariant. Each image is compact. The open balls $\{z:|z|_\ell<\ell^a\}$, $a\geq0$, cover $\mathbf Q_\ell$; a finite subcover of each image, followed by the maximum over the finitely many $i$, gives one $a\geq0$ with $|f_i(g)|_\ell\leq\ell^a$ for all $i,g$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $f_i'=\ell^a f_i$ takes values in $\mathbf Z_\ell$. As a map to this subspace with the valuation topology, it remains continuous, additive and conjugation-invariant.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: coordinate maps and uniform integral scaling

proof.text:
Apply the current statement of [lem-wf-additive-characters-h1] with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$. Its additional prime-to-characteristic hypothesis holds: if $p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)$, then $q=p^b$ for $b\geq1$, so $\ell
mid q$ implies $\ell
e p$. Its geometric connectedness, separatedness and finite-type hypotheses are precisely among those on $U_0$; its $U, ar u$ and degree-one lift are ours. Its valuation topology on $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is the subspace topology used in the preceding step. The isomorphism sends $f_i'$ to a compatible family $x_i\in\varprojlim_n H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)$. The stated Frobenius action is $f\mapsto[g\mapsto f(s^{-1}gs)]$, so the invariance of $f_i'$ implies $\Phi_q x_i=x_i$. All hypotheses of [prop-wf-open-curve-h1-no-frobenius-fixed], including normality, pure dimension one and $\ell
mid q$, are those of the target. It gives $x_i=0$. The additive isomorphism is injective, hence $f_i'=0$. The scalar $\ell^a$ is nonzero, so $t_i\circ\lambda=0$ for every $i$. Coordinates separate points of $E$, giving $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: Frobenius-fixed compatible classes and vanishing

proof.text: To justify logarithm injectivity on the domain actually supplied in step 1, use [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, write $\ell=u\varpi^e$ with $u\in\mathcal O_E^\times$ and $e=v_E(\ell)>0$, and put $r=2e$. Since $\mathfrak m_E=\varpi\mathcal O_E$, multiplying principal ideals gives $\ell^2\mathcal O_E=\varpi^{2e}\mathcal O_E=\mathfrak m_E^{2e}$. For every prime $\ell$, including $\ell=2$, $r=2e>e/(\ell-1)$. Thus [lem-wf-deep-principal-unit-log] makes the logarithm injective on $1+\mathfrak m_E^r=1+\ell^2\mathcal O_E$. It is the same series as the logarithm in [lem-wf-compact-character-logarithm]. Since $\chi(g)^N$ belongs to that domain and $\lambda(g)=0=\log(1)$, injectivity gives $\chi(g)^N=1$ for every $g\in\Pi$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: injectivity; domain comparison from the cited DVR statement

proof.text: The image $\chi(\Pi)$ lies in the roots of the nonzero polynomial $T^N-1$ over the field $E$, hence has at most $N$ elements. Conversely, for a finite image its exponent (equal to $1$ for the trivial group) is a positive integer killing every image element.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: finite roots and the converse

proof_origin.place: Full proof, retaining the blueprint route; current hypothesis and logarithm-domain obligations expanded
